\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

Layer selection is a researcher degree of freedom that can reverse conclusions; the multi-metric audit protocol (\cref{sec:discussion}) mitigates this. Contribution~1 generalizes geometrically; Contribution~2 (+15--22pp precision) is cross-validated at 7--8B, exploratory at 32B$^\dagger$, and encoder-conditional; seven alternative methods fail (\cref{tab:negative}).\looseness=-1

1	Reasoning models with chain-of-thought (CoT) can self-jailbreak: their reasoning traces transition from safe deliberation to committed harmful generation without adversarial input. Detecting the commitment point (CP)---the first reasoning step after which safety deliberation permanently ceases---requires monitoring internal representations or generated text. We study four reasoning LLMs, primarily Qwen-based (3/4 models) with one Llama model for limited cross-architecture evidence, on HarmThoughts and provide initial characterization of hidden-state (HS) vs.\ text probe capabilities on this benchmark. The comparison depends critically on which transformer layer is monitored: a crossing-rate composite metric masks the HS advantage at 32B scale by selecting shallow layers where representation compression inflates threshold crossings. Threshold-based layer selection recovers HS precision gains of +19.2 to +21.9pp against MiniLM-384d (Holm-Bonferroni corrected; advantage is encoder-conditional and represents an upper bound); this advantage diminishes with stronger encoders (384d: 4/4 models pass HB $\to$ 1024d BGE-large: 1/4). The 7--8B results are cross-validated (nested CV): precision and balanced accuracy confirmed; R1-8B safe-trace false positive rate (FPR) is significant but seed-sensitive (3/5 seeds pass HB). The 32B results are exploratory$^\dagger$ ($^\dagger$\,sample-limited, $n \leq 20$): QwQ-32B is significant but suggestive of position-competitiveness; R1-32B shows a pattern consistent with position mediation and falls below minimum detectable effect. A three-layer ensemble provides metric-agnostic HS advantage matching the best individual metric (4/4 models, $p \leq 0.002$). Metric-induced layer selection bias is the robust methodological finding; the empirical HS advantage is conditional on encoder quality, model scale, and position control.

1	Reasoning models with chain-of-thought (CoT) can self-jailbreak: their reasoning traces transition from safe deliberation to committed harmful generation without adversarial input. Detecting the commitment point (CP)---the first reasoning step after which safety deliberation permanently ceases---requires monitoring internal representations or generated text. We study four reasoning LLMs, primarily Qwen-based (3/4 models) with one Llama model for limited cross-architecture evidence, on HarmThoughts and provide initial characterization of hidden-state (HS) vs.\ text probe capabilities on this benchmark. The comparison depends critically on which transformer layer is monitored: a crossing-rate composite metric masks the HS advantage at 32B scale by selecting shallow layers where representation compression inflates threshold crossings. Threshold-based layer selection recovers HS precision gains of +19.2 to +21.9pp against MiniLM-384d (Holm-Bonferroni corrected; advantage is encoder-conditional and represents an upper bound); this advantage diminishes with stronger encoders (384d: 4/4 models pass HB $\to$ 1024d BGE-large: 1/4). The 7--8B results are cross-validated (nested CV): precision and balanced accuracy confirmed; R1-8B safe-trace false positive rate (FPR) is significant but seed-sensitive (3/5 seeds pass HB). The 32B results are exploratory$^\dagger$ ($^\dagger$\,sample-limited, $n \leq 20$): QwQ-32B is significant but suggestive of position-competitiveness; R1-32B shows a pattern consistent with position mediation and falls below minimum detectable effect. A three-layer ensemble provides metric-agnostic HS advantage matching the best individual metric (4/4 models, $p \leq 0.002$). Metric-induced layer selection bias is the robust methodological finding; the empirical HS advantage is conditional on encoder quality, model scale, and position control.

lines: \section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}
\paragraph{Layer selection as researcher degree of freedom~\citep{gelman2013garden}.}

-Our five-metric ablation (\cref{sec:layer-results}) shows crossing rate reverses the central finding via shallow-layer compression (\cref{app:cosine_volatility}), architecture-independent across Llama/Qwen (\cref{tab:r18b_full_layer}). A random-label control on QwQ-32B reveals crossing rate retains its shallow preference in 100\% of random-label permutations (CR-composite: 80\%), while precision's deep preference collapses to 20\% (\cref{app:random_cp}): the crossing-rate shallow preference is geometric (persisting under random labels), while threshold-based deep selection requires genuine safety labels. Contribution~1 (layer bias) thus generalizes from geometry and is internally valid (split-half replication; \cref{app:split_half}); Contribution~2 (HS advantage) is sample-dependent. Threshold-based layers peak at L63/64~\citep{wollschlager2025geometry}; R1-32B selectivity is 3.0pp (\cref{app:control}), below the 5pp threshold~\citep{hewitt2019control}.\looseness=-1

+Our five-metric ablation (\cref{sec:layer-results}) shows crossing rate reverses the central finding via shallow-layer compression (\cref{app:cosine_volatility}), architecture-independent across Llama/Qwen (\cref{tab:r18b_full_layer}). A random-label control on QwQ-32B reveals crossing rate retains its shallow preference in 100\% of random-label permutations (CR-composite: 80\%), while precision's systematic deep preference dissolves under random labels (Shallow\% drops to 20\%, selections scatter across the full layer range; \cref{app:random_cp}): the crossing-rate shallow preference is geometric (persisting under random labels), while threshold-based deep selection requires genuine safety labels. Contribution~1 (layer bias) thus generalizes from geometry and is internally valid (split-half replication; \cref{app:split_half}); Contribution~2 (HS advantage) is sample-dependent. Threshold-based layers peak at L63/64~\citep{wollschlager2025geometry}; R1-32B selectivity is 3.0pp (\cref{app:control}), below the 5pp threshold~\citep{hewitt2019control}.\looseness=-1
\paragraph{Encoder-quality boundary.}

The HS advantage is significant against 384d MiniLM (cross-validated at 7--8B; exploratory at 32B) but attenuated against 1024d BGE-large (1/4 HB). PCA capacity matching preserves significance (+16.8 to +23.1pp), partial evidence against a pure capacity explanation. Whether stronger encoders~\citep{wang2024e5mistral,boxo2025linear_probes} close the gap bounds these claims' shelf life.\looseness=-1

\subsection{Negative Results}\label{sec:negative}

No alternative method consistently matches supervised probing (\cref{tab:negative}). BOCPD~\citep{adams2007bayesian}/CUSUM fail (0\% detection on 3/4 models; \cref{app:bocpd_config}); Mahalanobis distance yields near-zero separation; RepE~\citep{zou2023representation} is model-dependent (QwQ-32B BA 0.756 vs.\ R1-32B 0.559); MLP probes overfit; CCS misaligns with temporal structure; cross-model transfer fails. These failures define four requirements: the signal is directional, gradual, model-specific, and linearly separable. lines: \section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}
\paragraph{Layer selection as researcher degree of freedom~\citep{gelman2013garden}.}

-Our five-metric ablation (\cref{sec:layer-results}) shows crossing rate reverses the central finding via shallow-layer compression (\cref{app:cosine_volatility}), architecture-independent across Llama/Qwen (\cref{tab:r18b_full_layer}). A random-label control on QwQ-32B reveals crossing rate retains its shallow preference in 100\% of random-label permutations (CR-composite: 80\%), while precision's systematic deep preference dissolves under random labels (Shallow\% drops to 20\%, selections scatter across the full layer range; \cref{app:random_cp}): the crossing-rate shallow preference is geometric (persisting under random labels), while threshold-based deep selection requires genuine safety labels. Contribution~1 (layer bias) thus generalizes from geometry and is internally valid (split-half replication; \cref{app:split_half}); Contribution~2 (HS advantage) is sample-dependent. Threshold-based layers peak at L63/64~\citep{wollschlager2025geometry}; R1-32B selectivity is 3.0pp (\cref{app:control}), below the 5pp threshold~\citep{hewitt2019control}.\looseness=-1

Contribution~1 (layer bias) thus generalizes from geometry and is internally valid (split-half replication; \cref{app:split_half}); Contribution~2 (HS advantage) is sample-dependent. Threshold-based layers peak at L63/64~\citep{wollschlager2025geometry}; R1-32B selectivity is 3.0pp (\cref{app:control}), below the 5pp threshold~\citep{hewitt2019control}.\looseness=-2
\paragraph{Encoder-quality boundary.}

The HS advantage is significant against 384d MiniLM (cross-validated at 7--8B; exploratory at 32B) but attenuated against 1024d BGE-large (1/4 HB). PCA capacity matching preserves significance (+16.8 to +23.1pp), partial evidence against a pure capacity explanation. Whether stronger encoders~\citep{wang2024e5mistral,boxo2025linear_probes} close the gap bounds these claims' shelf life.\looseness=-1

\paragraph{Layer selection as researcher degree of freedom~\citep{gelman2013garden}.}

-Our five-metric ablation (\cref{sec:layer-results}) shows crossing rate reverses the central finding via shallow-layer compression (\cref{app:cosine_volatility}), architecture-independent across Llama/Qwen (\cref{tab:r18b_full_layer}). Contribution~1 (layer bias) thus generalizes from geometry and is internally valid (split-half replication; \cref{app:split_half}); Contribution~2 (HS advantage) is sample-dependent. Threshold-based layers peak at L63/64~\citep{wollschlager2025geometry}; R1-32B selectivity is 3.0pp (\cref{app:control}), below the 5pp threshold~\citep{hewitt2019control}.\looseness=-2
\paragraph{Encoder-quality boundary.}

The HS advantage is significant against 384d MiniLM (cross-validated at 7--8B; exploratory at 32B) but attenuated against 1024d BGE-large (1/4 HB). PCA capacity matching preserves significance (+16.8 to +23.1pp), partial evidence against a pure capacity explanation. Whether stronger encoders~\citep{wang2024e5mistral,boxo2025linear_probes} close the gap bounds these claims' shelf life.\looseness=-1

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   This session continued from a previous conversation. Four Director instructions were processed:
   - **Resolve page overflow** (carried over): Fix the ~2-line Conclusion spill onto page 9 from the previous session's "2 factual errors + 4 claim enhancements" patch

   - **AdvBench Contingency Templates**: Prepare 3 scenario-based draft templates (A: 5/5 replication, B: 3/5 partial, C: CR fails) with placeholders for Phase 3 experiment results, stored locally without committing

   - Paper Agent architecture: communicates with Director via `paper_agent_post_to_director`, not `main_agent_post_to_director`

   - Random CP control: pure crossing rate = 100% shallow, CR-composite = 80% shallow, precision = 20% (scattered, not deep-concentrated)
   - Precision range across all 4 models: R1-8B +20.1, OT-7B +21.9, QwQ +19.2, R1-32B +15.4 → range is +15.4 to +21.9pp

file.content: Reasoning models with chain-of-thought (CoT) can self-jailbreak: their reasoning traces transition from safe deliberation to committed harmful generation without adversarial input. Detecting the commitment point (CP)---the first reasoning step after which safety deliberation permanently ceases---requires monitoring internal representations or generated text. We study four reasoning LLMs, primarily Qwen-based (3/4 models) with one Llama model for limited cross-architecture evidence, on HarmThoughts and provide initial characterization of hidden-state (HS) vs.\ text probe capabilities on this benchmark. The comparison depends critically on which transformer layer is monitored: a crossing-rate composite metric masks the HS advantage at 32B scale by selecting shallow layers where representation compression inflates threshold crossings. Threshold-based layer selection recovers HS precision gains of +15.4 to +21.9pp against MiniLM-384d (Holm-Bonferroni corrected; advantage is encoder-conditional and represents an upper bound); this advantage diminishes with stronger encoders (384d: 4/4 models pass HB $\to$ 1024d BGE-large: 1/4). The 7--8B results are cross-validated (nested CV): precision and balanced accuracy confirmed; R1-8B safe-trace false positive rate (FPR) is significant but seed-sensitive (3/5 seeds pass HB). The 32B results are exploratory$^\dagger$ ($^\dagger$\,sample-limited, $n \leq 20$): QwQ-32B is significant but suggestive of position-competitiveness; R1-32B shows a pattern consistent with position mediation and falls below minimum detectable effect. A three-layer ensemble provides metric-agnostic HS advantage matching the best individual metric (4/4 models, $p \leq 0.002$). Metric-induced layer selection bias is the robust methodological finding; the empirical HS advantage is conditional on encoder quality, model scale, and position control.

\paragraph{Cross-dataset validation.}
We replicate the layer selection analysis on AdvBench~\citep{advbench} ({{ADVBENCH_N_TRACES}} traces, {{ADVBENCH_N_JAILBREAK}} jailbreaks) using {{ADVBENCH_MODEL}}. The CR-composite metric again selects a shallow layer (L{{ADVBENCH_CR_LAYER_32B}}) while threshold-based metrics converge on L{{ADVBENCH_THRESH_LAYER_32B}}, confirming that the metric-induced layer divergence generalizes beyond HarmThoughts. At the threshold-based layer, HS precision advantage is +{{ADVBENCH_PREC_DELTA}}pp ($p{{ADVBENCH_PREC_P}}$), consistent with HarmThoughts (\cref{tab:advbench_layer_selection}).\looseness=-1

\section{AdvBench Cross-Dataset Validation}\label{app:advbench}

We validate our central findings on AdvBench~\citep{advbench}, an adversarial benchmark with {{ADVBENCH_N_TRACES}} traces ({{ADVBENCH_N_JAILBREAK}} successful jailbreaks). CP annotations follow the same protocol as HarmThoughts (first permanent cessation of safety deliberation). We evaluate {{ADVBENCH_MODEL}} with the same five metrics and seven window sizes.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\caption{AdvBench layer selection: {{ADVBENCH_MODEL}}. CR-composite selects shallow layers; threshold-based metrics select deep layers, consistent with HarmThoughts.}
\label{tab:advbench_layer_selection}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
\textbf{Metric} & \textbf{Layer} & \textbf{Depth (\%)} \\
\midrule
CR-composite & L{{ADVBENCH_CR_LAYER_32B}} & {{ADVBENCH_CR_SHALLOW_PCT}}\% \\
Precision & L{{ADVBENCH_THRESH_LAYER_32B}} & {{ADVBENCH_THRESH_DEPTH_PCT}}\% \\
Inverse FPR & L{{ADVBENCH_THRESH_LAYER_32B}} & {{ADVBENCH_THRESH_DEPTH_PCT}}\% \\
Additive composite & L{{ADVBENCH_THRESH_LAYER_32B}} & {{ADVBENCH_THRESH_DEPTH_PCT}}\% \\
Balanced accuracy & L{{ADVBENCH_BA_LAYER}} & {{ADVBENCH_BA_DEPTH_PCT}}\% \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\caption{AdvBench HS vs.\ text comparison at threshold-based layer for {{ADVBENCH_MODEL}}.}
\label{tab:advbench_hs_text}
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
\textbf{Metric} & \textbf{HS} & \textbf{Text} & $\Delta$ \\
\midrule
Precision & {{ADVBENCH_HS_PREC}} & {{ADVBENCH_TEXT_PREC}} & +{{ADVBENCH_PREC_DELTA}} \\
Balanced Acc. & {{ADVBENCH_HS_BA}} & {{ADVBENCH_TEXT_BA}} & +{{ADVBENCH_BA_DELTA}} \\
FPR & {{ADVBENCH_HS_FPR}} & {{ADVBENCH_TEXT_FPR}} & {{ADVBENCH_FPR_DELTA}} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The layer divergence (L{{ADVBENCH_CR_LAYER_32B}} vs.\ L{{ADVBENCH_THRESH_LAYER_32B}}) is {{ADVBENCH_LAYER_GAP}} layers, comparable to the {{HARMTHOUGHTS_LAYER_GAP}}-layer gap observed on HarmThoughts. All five metrics replicate their HarmThoughts ranking, confirming that the metric-induced bias is dataset-independent.

\section{Partial Cross-Dataset Evidence (AdvBench)}\label{app:advbench}

We evaluate layer selection on AdvBench~\citep{advbench} ({{ADVBENCH_N_TRACES}} traces, {{ADVBENCH_N_JAILBREAK}} jailbreaks) using {{ADVBENCH_MODEL}}. The CR-composite metric selects L{{ADVBENCH_CR_LAYER_32B}} (shallow), consistent with HarmThoughts. Threshold-based metrics converge on L{{ADVBENCH_THRESH_LAYER_32B}} (deep), replicating the metric-induced layer divergence. However, the HS advantage is metric-dependent: precision replicates (+{{ADVBENCH_PREC_DELTA}}pp, $p{{ADVBENCH_PREC_P}}$), while {{ADVBENCH_UNSTABLE_METRICS}} show instability ({{ADVBENCH_UNSTABLE_DETAIL}}). This partial replication is consistent with HarmThoughts findings where FPR and BA showed greater sensitivity to sample composition than precision (\cref{sec:hs-text}).

%% 位置: discussion.tex, "Encoder-quality boundary" 段落末尾

%%
%% 原文:
%%   The HS advantage is significant against 384d MiniLM ... shelf
%%   life.\looseness=-1
%%
%% 替换为:
The HS advantage is significant against 384d MiniLM (cross-validated at 7--8B; exploratory at 32B) but attenuated against 1024d BGE-large (1/4 HB). PCA capacity matching preserves significance (+16.8 to +23.1pp), partial evidence against a pure capacity explanation. Partial AdvBench replication (precision replicates; {{ADVBENCH_UNSTABLE_METRICS}} unstable; \cref{app:advbench}) suggests FPR/BA instability is not HarmThoughts-specific. Whether stronger encoders~\citep{wang2024e5mistral,boxo2025linear_probes} close the gap bounds these claims' shelf life.\looseness=-1


%% --- B3. Conclusion/Introduction 不修改 ---
%% "one benchmark" 限定保持, 因为 AdvBench 只是 partial evidence

Converging evidence (oracle analysis, PCA capacity control, control task selectivity, position residualization) supports genuine safety representations, but causal validation via DAS~\citep{geiger2025causal}, ITI~\citep{li2024iti}, or circuit breakers~\citep{zou2024improving} is needed. Under linear residualization, 3/4 models retain significant non-positional HS advantage; under quadratic control, only 2/4 (QwQ-32B absorbed by $(t/T)^2$; \cref{tab:position_quadratic}). Quadratic control risks overfitting at $n{=}17$--$20$, so the divergent results bracket the true position contribution; HS probes partly functioning as better position encoders remains unexcluded. We propose a multi-metric audit protocol: compute ${\geq}3$ metrics, flag disagreement, and verify cosine volatility (\cref{app:cosine_volatility,app:deployment_operating_points}). Cross-dataset generalization of both the layer bias and HS advantage remains an open question requiring benchmarks with independent CP annotations.\looseness=-1

\section{Representation Compression Analysis}
\label{app:cosine_volatility}

We measure step-to-step cosine distance at CR-composite (shallow) vs.\ threshold-based (deep) layers across all models to characterize the compression mechanism underlying the crossing rate bias (\cref{tab:cosine_volatility}).

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\caption{Step-to-step cosine distance at CR-composite (shallow) and threshold-based (deep) layers. Shallow layers produce highly compressed representations (1.4--2.7$\times$ smaller inter-step distances).}
\label{tab:cosine_volatility}
\begin{tabular}{llcc}
\toprule
\textbf{Model} & \textbf{Layer (type)} & \textbf{Mean} & \textbf{Std} \\
\midrule

 & L14 (thresh.) & 0.411 & 0.143 \\[2pt]
OT-7B & L2 (CR-comp.) & 0.077 & 0.080 \\

QwQ-32B & L2 (CR-comp.) & 0.037 & 0.064 \\
 & L63 (thresh.) & 0.084 & 0.056 \\[2pt]
R1-32B & L10 (CR-comp.) & 0.067 & 0.050 \\
 & L63 (thresh.) & 0.092 & 0.076 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Shallow layers produce highly compressed representations: consecutive steps cluster within small cosine distances (0.04--0.19), while deep-layer representations spread more widely (0.09--0.41). Inter-step distances at shallow layers are 1.4--2.7$\times$ smaller than at deep layers across all models. A linear probe operating in this compressed space sits near the noise floor, where minor numerical fluctuations produce spurious threshold crossings that inflate crossing rate independently of discriminative power. Deep layers produce well-separated representations where crossings correspond to genuine semantic transitions.
